featured_reviews.review_text: I visited with my family on Christmas eve and I felt very happy. There was beautiful decoration all around the church too. featured_reviews.name: Joseph D'Cruz
featured_reviews.review_text: This is one of the oldest places in Vakola. This Catholic parish was very large (in terms of members) in the 80's and 90's with almost 30000 families being part of it but due to cost of living going up and real-estate prices going through the roof many have sold their places and moved to the suburbs. Currently the numbers have come down to almost close to 10000 or little above that. Still one of the very active churches in terms of people's participation. There are 5 resident priests allotted to this parish. There's also boys school run by the parish. A very spiritual place and the services are conducted with a lot of vigour and enthusiasm. Truly fulfilling to be part of those.

featured_reviews.name: Divya Alisha Mathews
featured_reviews.review_text: This is a non-denominational church. A few years ago I was looking out for a church. I wanted the Holy Spirit to tell me which church I should be in. So one Sunday, I walked into ARH and I immediately felt the tangible  presence of God. Holy Spirit confirmed it to me in my spirit that I should remain here. It has taught me to linger in God's presence and to grow spiritually day by day.  It teaches about the love Jesus demonstrated on the cross. And this non-judgmental love is reflected as you walk through the doors of ARH. In fact, anyone who knows God and His Word well will recognize the genuine love and worship overflowing in this place. The pastors here are anointed people of God. They are very humble and they teach the Word of God with such simplicity that anyone can understand. This church never hides their passion for God. Love love love being a part of ARH.

featured_reviews.review_text: The St. Andrew's Church at Bandra is a heritage church which is over 400 years old. The church was recently renovated and it looks better than ever. featured_reviews.name: Joseph Nunes
featured_reviews.review_text:
St. Andrew’s Church, with its 400+ years of rich history, has recently undergone a transformative 20-month renovation that beautifully preserves its heritage while rejuvenating its spiritual ambiance.

✨ Architectural Revival
Façade and Roof Rejuvenation: Heritage specialists like Jivraj Sankhat and Savani Heritage Conservation expertly restored the church’s iconic roof, façade, marble, woodwork, and stained-glass windows, reviving their original splendor.

Traditional Techniques: The renovation prioritized authenticity. Over 5.5 ft thick walls were replastered with lime instead of cement—an effort to maintain the church’s historical integrity.

🌞 Rediscovered Beauty
Choir Loft & Lighting: Long-hidden architectural gems, such as the choir loft’s clerestory windows, were uncovered—reintroducing natural light into the nave and restoring a key visual element of the original design.

💒 Interior Elegance
Faithfully Restored Altars: The Portuguese-inspired altars, once scarred by moisture and termite damage, were carefully conserved and revived to their former glory.

Wooden Pulpit Revival: Carved with biblical narrative, the original pulpit was meticulously restored, complete with its ornate canopy—allowing worshippers to once more feel its spiritual resonance.

⏳ Heritage Sensitivity & Community Effort
Meticulous, Not Hasty: From April 2024 to December 2025, the renovation focused on preservation over superficial repairs—respecting the church’s Portuguese colonial architecture.

Community-Driven, Funded by Love: Entirely financed by parishioners and diaspora support, the project faced financial hurdles—yet the community’s unwavering commitment ensured the work reached its homestretch.

🎖 A Joyous Reopening
On a beautiful Sunday evening, over a thousand worshippers celebrated the church’s rededication—blessed by Cardinal Oswald Gracias—marking a poignant return to its rightful spiritual grandeur.

In summary, the recent renovations at St. Andrew’s Church masterfully balance respect for its centuries-old heritage with modern integrity. From the reimagined façade to the restored interior treasures, every detail reflects love, care, and unwavering faith. It’s a testament to what can be achieved when a community unites to preserve its legacy—and a spiritually uplifting sanctuary reborn.

featured_reviews.name: Partha S Mondal
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount popularly known as Mount Mary Church is a historic Roman Catholic shrine in Bandra, Mumbai, perched on a foot hill overlooking the Arabian Sea. Known for its neo-Gothic architecture and 16th-century statue of the Virgin Mary, it is a major pilgrimage center drawing people of all faiths.

Many visitors come to Mount St Mary Church in order to make their mannat wish come true.

Place is very well maintained.

featured_reviews.name: Gaurav
featured_reviews.review_text: The Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount (Mount Mary Church) in Bandra is a beautiful and peaceful place with great spiritual significance. The architecture is stunning, and the atmosphere is calm and soothing. Located near Bandstand, it also offers lovely views of the sea. The church is very well maintained and attracts people of all faiths. During the annual Mount Mary Fair, the place becomes vibrant and lively. A must-visit landmark in Mumbai for peace, faith, and history.

featured_reviews.name: Anugraha Ghale
featured_reviews.review_text:
We arrived around 6 PM just as Mass was happening, and the church was beautifully filled with people, a mix of locals and visitors. Even though we didn’t stay for the full service or take part in any activities, it was lovely just to sit for a moment and take in the serenity. The architecture is stunning, especially as the evening light hits the façade.

Bandra itself is such an interesting part of Mumbai a blend of old Portuguese roots, coastal charm, and modern city rhythm. The basilica, built during the 16th century by the Portuguese, still carries traces of that heritage in its architecture and stone walls. You can almost feel how it’s stood as an anchor through centuries of storms, festivals, and city life. Don’t miss 10 min walk to the fort!

featured_reviews.name: Sushil kumar kushwaha
featured_reviews.review_text:
Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount Church situated atop Mount Mary, Bandra West is one of the most revered churches in Mumbai.
Mary Church is the statue of Our Lady of the Mount, also known as the Mother Mary. It is a spiritual sanctuary built in semi Gothic style.
The architecture combines grandeur with serenity and offers a visually rich and spiritually enriching experience for visitors.
An older structure housing the original statue of Mary, and nearby is the Our Lady of Fatima Oratory, built in 1954, featuring a marble statue of Our Lady of Fatima and the message of Fatima.
Prayer times typically run from early morning (around 5:30 AM) to evening (7:30 PM) on weekdays and Sundays,
The Church attracts devotees from all faiths for its belief in miracles, with many lighting candles in thanksgiving for favors granted !!!

featured_reviews.name: Shakeel Ahmed
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount, colloquially known as Mount Bandra and Mount St Mary Church; is a basilica (shrine) of the Roman Catholic Church, located at the Bandra neighbourhood of Bombay (Mumbai), India.

The story of Mount Mary Church in Bandra begins in the 1570s when Jesuit priests built a small mud-and-stone oratory on a hill overlooking the Arabian Sea in Bandra. They brought a statue of Our Lady to this location, and this event marked the beginning of the shrine's history.

The original statue is believed to have been miraculously recovered after being thrown into the sea, and a more permanent basilica was later built on the site, which has become a place of pilgrimage and peace for people of all faiths, particularly Hindus and Christians. The current church, a semi-Gothic structure, was rebuilt in 1904 and is now known as the Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount.
